land.text: Xu's heartland, 'conquered by Wu in 512 BC'; King Zhangyu surrendered and 'Hereby, Xu was extinguished'

successors.note: Zhangyu and his followers went into exile in Chu (Xu page). The Chu dossier (chu.json) records Chu annexing Xu in 512 from the Chu page's list; the Xu page gives Wu.

capitals.name: Xu (Sihong County)
capitals.note: 'The capital of Xu was located in Sihong County'; modern Pizhou (about 117.95E, 34.3N) was its ritual center and necropolis. The coordinates of Sihong are the researcher's placing; the page earlier says Xu 'moved its core area further south into northern Anhui'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 750 shape plus the capital Sihong and the ritual centre Pizhou

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's first Xu shape: 'Xu's existence is first reliably reported by the Yi Zhou Shu for 1042 BC', centred on 'northern Jiangsu and Anhui' with a capital at Sihong and a ritual centre at Pizhou. The shape is Cliopatria's 750 shape (22 cells north of the Huai) with 60 km round Sihong and 30 km round Pizhou added; the page gives no boundary or area, and says Xu 'controlled much of the Huai River valley' at its height (944).

correction.text: the Xu heartland: Cliopatria's 750 shape plus Sihong and Pizhou, valid -750..-512

keyframe_review.note: 4,637 km2 for -750..-451 in Cliopatria, a small block (34.4-35.1N) on the Xuzhou-Tengzhou plain that misses the capital at Sihong (33.5N). Correction: add the Sihong and Pizhou areas, and end the shape in 512, when 'Xu was eventually conquered by Wu in 512 BC' (infobox 'Conquered by Wu: 512 BC'), 'reduced to its heartland'. No infobox area exists, so the area check cannot be made.

correction.text: no Xu after 512: the page ends the state with the Wu conquest

keyframe_review.note: The page ends Xu in 512 ('Hereby, Xu was extinguished'; infobox 'Conquered by Wu: 512 BC') and mentions no Warring States Xu ('The page doesn't discuss Xu in the Warring States period'), so the 15-cell shape of -450..-285 has no support. In Cliopatria its cells are former Teng (10) and Zhu (5) land, and 20 cells of the old Xu shape pass to Song in 450. Correction: draw nothing as Xu from 511; the land is Wu's (512), then Yue's after 473 (Wu page).

region.text: northern Jiangsu and Anhui round the capital at Sihong

ledger.note: c. 1042: the Xu of the Huai River valley first appear in the record, in the Rebellion of the Three Guards against the Duke of Zhou. 'Xu's existence is first reliably reported by the Yi Zhou Shu for 1042 BC'; infobox 'Established: Unknown', foundation stories 'remain legendary'. The page says Xu was 'centered in northern Jiangsu and Anhui'; the year is the first report, not a founding.

512: Wu conquers Xu and the state ends. Infobox 'Conquered by Wu: 512 BC'; 'Reduced to its heartland, Xu was eventually conquered by Wu in 512 BC' (King Helü, citing the Zuo Zhuan); King Zhangyu surrendered, 'Hereby, Xu was extinguished', and his followers went into exile in Chu. The Spring and Autumn table: 'Xu 512 BCE: to Wu'.

wars.name: Zhou subjugation of the Huai valley (Rebellion of the Three Guards)
wars.outcome: Xu 'participated in the Rebellion of the Three Guards against the Duke of Zhou'; Zhou forces subjugated the Huai valley in 1039.
wars.note: Before Cliopatria's first Xu shape; no contest is drawn.

wars.name: Xu-led Huaiyi coalition against Zhou
wars.outcome: 'By 944 BC, Lord Yan of Xu managed to unite thirty-six Dongyi and Huaiyi states'; the Zhou 'could not re-subjugate the Huaiyi' and accepted their independence; the Huaiyi counter-offensive of 850 collapsed; King Xuan's campaign of 822 ended in a minor Zhou victory or a peace.
wars.note: Dates are the page's scattered ones (944, 850, 822); all before Cliopatria's Xu.

wars.name: Chu invasion of Xu and Battle of Loulin
wars.outcome: 'Chu retaliated in 645 BC, and launched an invasion of Xu'; Qi's coalition failed to relieve Xu at Loulin, but Xu survived, weakened.

wars.name: Wu conquest of Xu
wars.outcome: Wu under King Helü besieged Xu; King Zhangyu surrendered and Xu was extinguished.

certainty.note: Xu's extent is known from bronzes and a few city names; the Huai valley frontier of 944 is the widest and least certain.

sources.title: Xu (state)
sources.note: Identity, Sihong capital, 1042 first report, 944/850/822/645 episodes, 512 conquest by Wu; no Warring States Xu; no area.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Xu' (-750..-285) is split: the first shape is Xu until 512 (moved south to the capital and extended back to 1042); the three Warring States rows are marked wrong. Possible explanation of those rows: Cliopatria's second Xu sits on Teng and Zhu land (Shandong), which suggests a different Xu or a mis-assigned polygon. Chu's dossier annexes Xu in 512 from the Chu page's list while the Xu page has Wu as conqueror and exile in Chu; the Wu dossier takes the conquest. Not opened (budget): Wu's 512 campaign in detail, the Huaiyi page, pages on Xu bronzes. The Cliopatria area 4,637 km2 cannot be compared with an infobox (none). Gazetteer names needed: Sihong, Pizhou (coordinates are used meanwhile).
